# The Problem

- The data science ecosystem has been moving steadily towards using Apache Arrow (Arrow), a standard for in memory representation of arrays and tables.
- The spatial data science ecosystem is no different, and is moving faster than other parts of the data science ecosystem in its adoption of Arrow and GeoArrow.
- Standardizing on Arrow as a format simplifies the data transfer between processes allowing tools to avoid expensive serializtion and deserialization steps to convert one in memory representation to another
- GeoArrow is an extension of the Arrow standard that defines how spatial data can be represented in memory to be compatible with Arrow.
- The most utilized spatial library in the world, GDAL, has begun supporting GeoArrow and Arrow
- Python's ubiquitous pandas library has adopted Arrow and the spatial extension, geopandas, too, has begun adopting GeoArrow
- R's support of geoarrow is limited.
- Notably, the geoarrow R package provides an R-native representation of GeoArrow arrays that is compatible with standard data.frames, {arrow} R package, and {nanoarrow}.
- Recent ISC funded work has also focused on GeoArrow too improved this via https://github.com/r-spatial/geoarrowWidget which supports sending geoarrow across the wire from R into the browser.


- However, there remains no native GeoArrow computation engine.
- Spatial data scientists in R still utilize {sf} which, unfortunately, does not scale sufficiently.
 - In part, because geometries are stored as R list objets and converted to and from GEOS and S2 geometries whenever calculations occur.
- There has been recent developments in the spatial ecosystem such as {duckspatial} and {sedonadb}
- However, neither of these libraries work with native R data.frames
{duckspatial} requires installing an external duckdb spatial extension which is 57mb on a MBP M5
{sedonadb} is not published on CRAN
{geoarrowrs} is completely dependency free, a 14mb installation, and is targeting full coverage of

We need highly performant in-memory spatial operations
